newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian firm called Sins wins Sibneft oil tender.
newsitem.headline: Russian firm called Sins wins Sibneft oil tender.

text.p: A Russian company called Sins won an investment tender for a 19 percent stake in Russia's Sibneft oil company on Friday, according to a company which controls Sibneft.

ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) Chief Executive Ivan Kulikov told Reuters that Sins outbid the tender's other participant, the Stens company, with a bid exceeding the minimum $43.48 million starting price by $1.5 million.
Under the terms of the tender, Sins is required to invest this amount in the oil company.
In addition, Sins paid almost 82.38 billion roubles ($15.3 million) for the shares, which are not actively traded.
Kulikov declined to provide details on Sins and Stens, which appear to be front companies for one or more major Russian corporations.
NFK and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii won the right to manage a 51 percent stake in Sibneft in a shares-for-loans auction late last year.
OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya is one of Russia's dozen or so vertically-integrated oil companies.
Foreigners are restricted to a 15 percent stake in the company, which is likely to be sold by the end of October.
Sibneft's main crude oil production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz of which it owns 38 percent. It also owns, among other companies, the Omsk refinery.
